findings.issue_text: `.panel { margin-left: auto }` does not pin the panel to the far edge in RTL locales — under `direction: rtl` the flex row reverses, the auto margin absorbs space already on that side, and header controls (search, user menu, hamburger) render mid-header next to the title and get squeezed instead of hugging the inline-end edge; fix with the logical property `margin-inline-start: auto` or a `[dir="rtl"]` override (header.scss:35-40)

Old-spec flexbox fallbacks emitted by `@mixin flexbox()` (`display: -webkit-box`/`-moz-box`/`-ms-flexbox`) cannot reproduce the layout — the `margin-left: auto` pinning technique doesn't exist in the 2009 spec (which distributes space via `box-pack`, not auto margins) and IE10's `-ms-flexbox` auto-margin support is unreliable, so the panel renders immediately after the title instead of pinned right in exactly the browsers the shims target; either the old-spec display lines are dead weight or the layout needs a fallback (mixins.scss:96-102, header.scss:37)

`align-items()` mixin omits `-moz-box-align` while the other mixins shim Firefox (`flexbox()` emits `display: -moz-box` and `order()` emits `-moz-box-ordinal-group`) — in 2009-spec Mozilla engines `.contents`/`.small-action` get the default `box-align: stretch` instead of `center`, so header items and small-action rows stretch to full container height instead of centering (mixins.scss:111-117)

mixins.scss align-items mixin (~line 100): legacy prefixes (-webkit-box-align, -ms-flex-align) use 2009/2012 spec vocabulary where flex-start/flex-end are invalid (they require start/end), so future callers passing flex-start would silently lose those prefixed declarations in legacy engines
mixins.scss align-items mixin: -ms-align-items is not a real property in any browser, making it a dead declaration

topic.scss @include order(2) on .extra-info-wrapper only has effect if its parent is a flex container; the diff doesn't show the DOM so it can't be verified the parent is the now-flex .contents — if it isn't, the declaration is inert; worth a visual smoke test of the header with extra info visible

Legacy flexbox branch is a silent false-pass: `margin-left: auto` has no space-distributing meaning in the legacy 2009 box model that the `flexbox()`/`order()` mixins explicitly target (mixins.scss:100-131 + header.scss:37), so on engines taking the `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` branch the panel renders flush against the title instead of right-aligned and content is top-aligned instead of centered; additionally `align-items()` emits `-webkit-box-align` but omits `-moz-box-align` (old Firefox loses vertical centering), and `-ms-align-items` is not a real property (dead line)

`.extra-info-wrapper` flex item can push the header panel off-screen with user-controlled content (topic.scss:29-32 + header.scss:14-19, 35-40): with default `min-width: auto` and no `flex-wrap`, a long unbreakable token (e.g., a URL) in the user-authored topic title sets min-content width larger than available space, `margin-left: auto` on `.panel` collapses to 0, and the row overflows horizontally — pushing header navigation controls (search, user menu, hamburger, login) partially or fully outside the viewport, a regression from the float layout where `.panel { float: right }` stayed anchored at the right edge

`.small-action-desc` silently changes from full-width block to shrink-to-fit flex item and all vertical rhythm is removed (topic-post.scss:263-265, 279-280, 289-292, 302-304): as a flex item with default `flex: 0 1 auto` it shrink-wraps to content width so right-floated/right-aligned date/meta elements lose their anchor and reflow next to the text; and deletion of every vertical spacing mechanism (`padding: 0.5em 0` → 0, `margin-top: 5px` removed, inner `p { margin: 5px 0 }` → 0, `> p { padding-top: 4px }` removed) leaves multi-paragraph content with zero inter-paragraph spacing, visually merging paragraphs

goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `.panel { margin-left: auto }` does not pin the panel to the far edge in RTL locales — under `direction: rtl` the flex row reverses, the auto margin absorbs space already on that side, and header controls (search, user menu, hamburger) render mid-header next to the title and get squeezed instead of hugging the inline-end edge; fix with the logical property `margin-inline-start: auto` or a `[dir="rtl"]` override (header.scss:35-40)

adjudication.rationale: In `header.scss` the `.panel` layout was changed from `float: right;` to a flex item with `margin-left: auto;` inside a new flex container (`.contents` now includes `@include flexbox()`). Using a physical `margin-left` is inherently LTR-biased; a logical property (`margin-inline-start`) or an RTL override would be more robust for RTL layouts. However, the diff alone does not show that `direction: rtl` is used/supported in this codepath, so the claimed broken RTL rendering cannot be strictly verified from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Old-spec flexbox fallbacks emitted by `@mixin flexbox()` (`display: -webkit-box`/`-moz-box`/`-ms-flexbox`) cannot reproduce the layout — the `margin-left: auto` pinning technique doesn't exist in the 2009 spec (which distributes space via `box-pack`, not auto margins) and IE10's `-ms-flexbox` auto-margin support is unreliable, so the panel renders immediately after the title instead of pinned right in exactly the browsers the shims target; either the old-spec display lines are dead weight or the layout needs a fallback (mixins.scss:96-102, header.scss:37)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `@mixin flexbox()` with legacy `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` / `-ms-flexbox` fallbacks (mixins.scss) and simultaneously changes the header layout to rely on `margin-left: auto` on `.panel` (header.scss) instead of `float: right`. Those legacy flexbox specs don’t consistently support auto-margin space distribution the way modern flex does, so the prefixed display lines may not preserve the intended “pin right” behavior. Whether this is a user-visible bug depends on whether those older engines are actually in scope, but the incompatibility/dead-weight concern is real and grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `align-items()` mixin omits `-moz-box-align` while the other mixins shim Firefox (`flexbox()` emits `display: -moz-box` and `order()` emits `-moz-box-ordinal-group`) — in 2009-spec Mozilla engines `.contents`/`.small-action` get the default `box-align: stretch` instead of `center`, so header items and small-action rows stretch to full container height instead of centering (mixins.scss:111-117)

adjudication.rationale: In mixins.scss the new `@mixin align-items($alignment)` outputs `-webkit-box-align`, `-webkit-align-items`, `-ms-flex-align`, `-ms-align-items`, and `align-items`, but omits `-moz-box-align` (lines shown in the diff). Since `@mixin flexbox()` still emits `display: -moz-box` and `@mixin order()` emits `-moz-box-ordinal-group`, the mixins are explicitly targeting old Mozilla 2009 flexbox; without `-moz-box-align`, those engines won’t apply the intended centering, falling back to the default align behavior for `-moz-box` (typically stretch). This can cause misalignment in `.contents` / `.small-action` where `@include align-items(center)` was added.

adjudication_records.issue_text: mixins.scss align-items mixin (~line 100): legacy prefixes (-webkit-box-align, -ms-flex-align) use 2009/2012 spec vocabulary where flex-start/flex-end are invalid (they require start/end), so future callers passing flex-start would silently lose those prefixed declarations in legacy engines

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `@mixin align-items($alignment)` that applies the same `$alignment` token to legacy properties `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align` (in `mixins.scss`). Those legacy specs use `start`/`end` rather than `flex-start`/`flex-end`, so if a caller passes standard `flex-start`/`flex-end`, the prefixed declarations would be invalid and ignored in legacy engines. While current new call sites use `center`/`baseline`, the mixin itself is incorrect for common alignment values, making it a real defect introduced by this diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `@include order(2);` to `.extra-info-wrapper` in `topic.scss`, and `order` only affects flex items (i.e., when the parent is a flex container). The diff does not show the relevant parent/container styles or DOM structure for `.extra-info-wrapper`, so it’s not verifiable here whether this will have any effect or be inert; the suggested visual smoke test is a reasonable, diff-grounded review concern rather than a confirmed defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Legacy flexbox branch is a silent false-pass: `margin-left: auto` has no space-distributing meaning in the legacy 2009 box model that the `flexbox()`/`order()` mixins explicitly target (mixins.scss:100-131 + header.scss:37), so on engines taking the `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` branch the panel renders flush against the title instead of right-aligned and content is top-aligned instead of centered; additionally `align-items()` emits `-webkit-box-align` but omits `-moz-box-align` (old Firefox loses vertical centering), and `-ms-align-items` is not a real property (dead line)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces flexbox mixins that include legacy 2009 syntax (`display: -webkit-box; display: -moz-box;`) and then relies on modern flex behavior in `header.scss` (`.panel { margin-left: auto; }`) to push the panel to the right. Auto margins are not a reliable/defined space-distribution mechanism in the old `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` model, so the right-alignment can fail on engines that only support that branch. Also, the new `@mixin align-items` emits `-webkit-box-align` but not `-moz-box-align`, so when `display: -moz-box` applies, centering may be lost. Finally, `-ms-align-items` is indeed not a valid property (dead line), indicating the mixin’s cross-browser intent is flawed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `.extra-info-wrapper` flex item can push the header panel off-screen with user-controlled content (topic.scss:29-32 + header.scss:14-19, 35-40): with default `min-width: auto` and no `flex-wrap`, a long unbreakable token (e.g., a URL) in the user-authored topic title sets min-content width larger than available space, `margin-left: auto` on `.panel` collapses to 0, and the row overflows horizontally — pushing header navigation controls (search, user menu, hamburger, login) partially or fully outside the viewport, a regression from the float layout where `.panel { float: right }` stayed anchored at the right edge

adjudication.rationale: The diff converts layouts from floats to flexbox without adding any wrap/shrink safeguards: `header.scss` makes `.contents` a flex container (`@include flexbox()`), replaces `.panel { float: right }` with `margin-left: auto` and `order(3)`, and `topic.scss` makes `.extra-info-wrapper` an ordered flex item (`@include order(2)`). With default flex behavior (`flex-wrap: nowrap` and flex items having `min-width: auto`), a sibling containing long unbreakable content can refuse to shrink and cause horizontal overflow, which can push/clip the `.panel` controls off the viewport—an issue that wouldn’t occur the same way with the prior float-right anchoring. This risk is grounded in the flex changes shown, though the exact DOM context isn’t fully visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: `.small-action-desc` silently changes from full-width block to shrink-to-fit flex item and all vertical rhythm is removed (topic-post.scss:263-265, 279-280, 289-292, 302-304): as a flex item with default `flex: 0 1 auto` it shrink-wraps to content width so right-floated/right-aligned date/meta elements lose their anchor and reflow next to the text; and deletion of every vertical spacing mechanism (`padding: 0.5em 0` → 0, `margin-top: 5px` removed, inner `p { margin: 5px 0 }` → 0, `> p { padding-top: 4px }` removed) leaves multi-paragraph content with zero inter-paragraph spacing, visually merging paragraphs

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `.small-action` is changed to a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`), which makes `.small-action-desc` a flex item. Since `.small-action-desc` is not given any flex sizing (e.g. `flex: 1`), it will size based on its contents rather than behaving like a normal full-width block, which can alter anchoring/reflow of sibling elements within the same row. Separately and clearly verifiable, multiple vertical-spacing rules are removed/zeroed (`padding: 0.5em 0 ...` → `padding: 0 1.5%`, `margin-top: 5px` removed, inner `p { margin: 5px 0; }` → `margin: 0;`, and `> p { padding-top: 4px; }` removed), which can cause multi-paragraph content to visually merge. These are concrete layout/visual-regression risks introduced by the diff.
